subject: AZ Private Offer — triggered usage floor & reseller commission rebalance
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gridscale.io>
To: ethan_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AZ Private Offer - questions on volume triggers and reseller split

Ethan / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — GridScale is excited about Redwood's latency profile on Azure. Before we move to procurement, we need clarity on one structural point the reseller raised: how a mid-term volume floor trigger would affect channel commission and list-price passback.

Specifically: GridScale expects usage to ramp in Q2; their reseller (CloudPath Partners) wants a protection so that if monthly spend crosses a defined usage floor for two consecutive months we move to a lower list-price floor (i.e., a higher discount) but the reseller commission should be rebalanced (reduced) to reflect the larger volume. They asked for a clear formula we can audit.

Can you send a proposed formula and outline reconciliation cadence (monthly vs quarterly), and what evidence Redwood requires for the reseller to claim performance-related commission tranches?

I've attached our projected usage (GridScale_ProjectedUsage_Q2.xlsx) to help size the triggers.

Appreciate a short proposal so procurement can draft the amendment.

Thanks,
Liam
Senior Procurement Manager
GridScale

--
Attachment: GridScale_ProjectedUsage_Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 92KB)

From: ethan_park@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gridscale.io>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AZ Private Offer - questions on volume triggers and reseller split

Liam — thanks for the usage file, that helps. High level proposal below; attach a short draft we can iterate on.

Proposal (summary):
- Trigger: if billable Azure spend to Redwood > $500,000 in a calendar month for two consecutive months, the contract moves to the "lifted-list" pricing band for the following month (effectively a lower list price / higher customer discount).
- Commission rebalance: Reseller commission splits into two tranches: Base commission (paid on all consumption) + Performance tranche (paid only when monthly spend is below trigger). When the trigger condition is met for two months, performance tranche is suspended and base commission rate reduces by 40% for the duration of the lifted-list band.
- Reconciliation cadence: monthly usage reporting with a 60-day true-up window. Reconciliations will be invoice-level and require reseller-submitted invoices/PO references plus Redwood usage report for matching.

Example (for clarity):
- Normal month: base 8% + performance 4% = 12% total to reseller.
- Post-trigger band: total commission changes to base 4.8% (8% * 60%) and performance tranche suspended => effective total 4.8%.

Requested next steps:
1) Jordan, can you run margin impact for the attached GridScale ramp and confirm gross-to-net and list-price delta?
2) Irene, can legal draft the amendment language for the two-month consecutive trigger and the evidence clause?
3) Ben, ops: confirm we can produce invoice-level usage exports as required for audit.

I attached a short two-page proposal PDF (RDW_AZPO_proposal-draft.pdf) and linked the HubSpot deal. If GridScale prefers a different floor or percent reductions let us know — we can model alternatives.

Ethan Park
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: RDW_AZPO_proposal-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
Related: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/458

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: ethan_park@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AZ Private Offer - questions on volume triggers and reseller split

Quick notes on the proposal — good start. A few operational/finance cautions and one suggestion to make this auditable: 

1) Withholding & cap: recommend a max cap on performance tranche clawback at 6 months of backward reconciliation to avoid excessive retro liabilities.
2) Tax/treatment: confirm with tax that commission rebalancing won't create unexpected VAT/GST liabilities for reseller. We'll need the reseller's tax docs (W-9 / VAT id) on file.
3) Evidence: rather than reseller invoices (which can be aggregated), require invoice-line items with Redwood product SKU and a unique customer identifier. That lets us match to our usage records programmatically.
4) True-up window: 60 days ok, but ops must support automated exports day +7 of month-end. If we can't support that cadence, push to 90 days.

Suggested commission split (operationally simpler): base 7% + performance 5% (total 12%). On trigger, base drops to 4.2% (60% of base) and performance suspended. This gives clearer accounting entries.

Jordan — can you build the updated spreadsheet with GridScale ramp assumptions and the revenue waterfall? Attaching RDW_AZPO_updated-split.xlsx when ready.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gridscale.io>, ethan_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AZ Private Offer - questions on volume triggers and reseller split

Liam — looping back with an operationalized ask and next step. Per Ben and legal input from Irene, final recommended structure below.

Final recommended structure (for GridScale + CloudPath):
- Trigger band: two consecutive months above $500k triggers lifted-list for the 3rd month onward until two consecutive months < $500k.
- Commission: base 7% + performance 5% in normal band. On trigger, base reduces to 4.2% (60% of base) and performance tranche suspended while in the lifted-list band.
- Reconciliation: monthly reports from Redwood, reseller must submit invoice-line evidence within 60 days. Redwood will run automated SKU-to-customer matching; disputed items go to a dispute queue with 30-day SLA.
- Liability protection: cap retro true-up exposure at 6 months; any amounts beyond would require sales leadership sign-off.

Next steps to finalize:
1) Liam — confirm GridScale accepts the two-month consecutive trigger, the $500k threshold, and the base/perf split.
2) If accepted, I'll upload an amendment to DocuSign and include the updated revenue waterfall (RDW_AZPO_updated-split.xlsx).

If you want a lower threshold or different percent splits we can model quickly. Otherwise I'll prepare the docusign amendment for signature.

-Jordan
Senior Deal Manager, Redwood Inference
